chunks: Ahmad said, and some of our companions mentioned, from Abu Abdullah (AS), and Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Abu Basir, from al-'Abd al-Salih (AS) that he
said: 'If I were to take charge of the affairs of the people, I would teach them divorce, then no one who opposed would be brought to me except that I would cause him pain by striking.'

key_terms.الطَّلَاق: talaq — Islamic divorce; a legal act requiring precise conditions (pronouncement formula, waiting period 'iddah, witnesses) whose violation invalidates the divorce
key_terms.الْعَبْد الصَّالِح: al-'Abd al-Salih — 'the Righteous Servant,' an epithet of Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), the 7th Imam
key_terms.ضَرْب: striking/corporal punishment — used here to signify judicial enforcement of the law
key_terms.وَلِيتُ أَمْرَ النَّاسِ: to take charge of/be entrusted with the affairs of the people — a phrase indicating executive and judicial authority

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kazim say about teaching people the rules of divorce?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) asserts that if he were granted political authority over the community, he would enforce correct knowledge and practice of divorce law, and would physically punish those who violated it. This statement reflects the Imam's conviction that the community of his time had fallen into serious error regarding the rules of divorce, which in classical Islamic law are governed by detailed and exacting requirements. The chapter title — 'the people will not be set straight upon divorce except by the sword' — underscores the urgency and severity of the matter in the Imam's view.

en.hubeali: Ahmad said, and he mentioned one of our companions, from Abu Abdullahasws, and Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Al-Abd Al-Salihasws (7th Imamasws) having said: ‘If Iasws am entrusted with the affairs of the people, Iasws would teach them the divorce, then they would not come with anyone who opposed, except that Iasws would Obligate the whipping (on him)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad has said that certain persons of our people have narrated from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from the virtuous servant (of Allah) has said the following: “Had I been governing people
I would teach them how to finalize a divorce case and thereafter make the violators to suffer pain.’”
